caption: The starting point of the pivot: cloud and infrastructure at ~25% of revenue in the past, ~33% then, ~50% targeted; it reached 84% by Q2 FY2022 and 79% data center alone by Q2 FY2027.
Cavium doubled the stated addressable market from $8bn+ to $16bn+ and took combined revenue to $3.4bn annualized, the first of three SAM step-ups built by acquisition.
The economic case for leaving consumer: infrastructure sockets are 3-5 year design cycles, 7-10+ year product lives and single-sourced, against 12-month cycles and multi-sourcing in consumer.
The SAM ratchet in one chart: $8bn at the 2017 investor day, $16bn on the Cavium announcement, $18bn a year later with 5G and automotive still counted as upside.
The first articulation of what became custom compute: Arm servers, security and network offload, and artificial intelligence named as the emerging data center compute architectures.
The end-FY2022 target model: 6-8% revenue CAGR, >66% gross margin, >35% operating margin, >30% FCF. Revenue growth was beaten many times over; gross margin never reached 66%.
The SerDes ladder from 12 Gbps in 2011 to 224/112/56 Gbps at 5nm and 3nm in 2021. This one IP block is reused across custom ASICs, optical DSPs, retimers, AECs and switches.
The cloud opportunity as management framed it before AI: DPU wins at four tier-one clouds, ASIC designs ramping, >$4bn cloud SAM in FY2024 and a 10-15% share target.

Inphi lifted the SAM from $20bn to $23bn and the growth rate from 9% to 12%, with more than 70% of Inphi revenue from cloud and 5G. This bought the electro-optics franchise now guided to grow >70% in FY2027.
Four years of portfolio surgery in one exhibit: infrastructure moved from 38% of revenue in FY2017 to 84% by Q2 FY2022 while consumer fell from 62% to 16%.
Cloud design-win momentum doubled and pulled forward: incremental revenue raised from ~$400m to ~$800m and the timing moved from FY2025-26 into FY2024, three years before the AI ramp.
Management's own warning that the growth mix is margin-dilutive: data center sits below the corporate average gross margin, enterprise networking above it. Gross margin has declined every year since.
The last long-term model ever published, raised at successive investor days: 15-20% revenue CAGR, 64-66% gross margin, 38-40% operating margin. Realized FY2026 was 59.5% and 35.3%.
The AI revenue plan: ~$200m in FY2023 to >$2.5bn in FY2026, split connectivity versus custom compute. FY2026 data center revenue actually printed at $6.1bn.

The data center TAM as of 2024: $21bn (CY2023) to $75bn (CY2028) at 29%, with share expectations line by line (gain in custom compute and switching, maintain in interconnect and storage) against a 20% long-term target from ~10%.
Interconnect decomposed: $4.3bn to $13.9bn CY2023-CY2028, with AEC DSPs the fastest line at 59% and inside-data-center optical the largest at $7.1bn.

The custom customer base before it was ever named: three lettered customers, four programs (training accelerator, inference accelerator, Arm CPU, new accelerator) and ramp years of CY2025 and CY2026, at three of four US hyperscalers.
The TAM restatement: CY2028 raised from $75bn to $94bn in 14 months on an unchanged CY2023 base and an unchanged source list, with compute up 29% and interconnect up 37%.
Custom decomposed into XPU ($6.0bn to $40.8bn, 47% CAGR) and XPU attach ($0.6bn to $14.6bn, 90% CAGR). Attach goes from 9% to 26% of the custom market.

The only public statement of custom program economics: each XPU is multi-billion-dollar lifetime revenue over 18-24 months, each attach several hundred million over 2-4 years, across a $75bn pipeline of >50 opportunities at >10 customers.
The only disclosed split of data center revenue: FY2025's $4.2bn was ~$3.7bn cloud AI and ~$0.5bn on-premise, with custom above 25% of Q4 FY2025 and targeted above 50%.
The share path: ~10% of the data center market in CY2023, ~13% in CY2024, 20% targeted for CY2028. Twenty percent of $94bn implies $18.8bn of data center revenue alone.

How Marvell positions custom silicon against NVIDIA: a custom XPU sits under all four platform architectures, including the third-party NVLink Fusion one, with attach content rising toward full custom.
The switching-cost mechanism: 3-4 years elapse from a foundry process being enabled to a product shipping, and Marvell validates test-chip IP before customer programs start. N5P through A14.
The sharpest quantified IP claim in the deck set: custom dense SRAM at 17x the bandwidth per mm2 of the best available third-party SRAM, 50% lower area at equal bandwidth and 66% lower standby power.
The packaging generations that carry the custom roadmap: 2D at 1X density, 2.5D at 4X, 3.5D at 8X, and 4D/4.5D with integrated optics and copper at 16X.
The socket table: 18 custom compute sockets, 12 of them at the top four US hyperscalers (3 XPU plus 9 attach) and 6 at emerging hyperscalers. Concentration and the attach ratio in one exhibit.
What the $1.3bn Celestial AI acquisition bought: Photonic Fabric claimed at 30x the reach of passive copper, 4x bandwidth, 4x lower power, 4x lower latency at roughly the same cost.

The four commercial models Marvell now sells under: buy standard, partner (Marvell design with customer IP), build (customer design with Marvell IP), and integrate build-to-spec chiplets with partner chiplets and memory.

The current map of the franchise: scale across, out, up and in, from hundreds of kilometres to millimetres, with the product family sold at each distance. Scale-up is where Celestial AI, XConn, UALink and ESUN land.
